title: ilionx has no dominant vertical, and the research proposes job-posting analysis to resolve it
content:
ilionx is recorded as broad-based with no dominant vertical, and the research calls the vertical mix genuinely unclear rather than merely unlisted. That is a scoring problem, because the pilot routes leads by sector: a firm spread evenly across sectors has no vertical to be routed to.

The proposed resolution is job-posting analysis, which is a deliberate choice of instrument. A firm's own positioning material is written to look broad, whereas its open roles reveal which sectors it is actually staffing for. Reading hiring rather than marketing is the cheaper and more honest route to a vertical, and it can be done from the desk.

Meanwhile the platform side of the row is comparatively well filled in: Oracle, Microsoft and integration work. That is an occupied slot on the size-and-slot-occupancy rescore that produced this rank, and it sits alongside an OSS-portfolio screen that has still not been run. Both the vertical question and the screen are desk tasks, and both should close before ilionx is treated as a targeted lead.
